hints: Look closely at what each division of cell type P produces in the tree diagram, does P disappear or does it keep making more of itself plus a different cell?
Remember what stem cells in bone marrow do, they divide by mitosis to self-renew and also produce specialised blood cells.
walkthrough:
**Observe the division pattern**

Look at the top cell P. It divides to make one P and one Q. That P then divides again to make more P cells, while also making more Q cells.

So P is never used up, it is maintained through all three cycles.

**Apply the stem cell idea**

This is exactly how a stem cell behaves. It self-renews to keep the stem cell pool constant, and it differentiates to form specialised cells.

In bone marrow, haemopoietic stem cells do this to continuously make differentiated blood cells like red blood cells and white blood cells.

**Identify P and Q**

P must be the stem cell because it keeps copying itself. Q must be the differentiated cell because it is produced as the specialised product and does not divide further here.

That matches row D.

options.A: Not correct. P is not a cancer cell dividing uncontrollably, it shows controlled self-renewal plus formation of a different cell type.
options.B: Not correct. P is not a cancer cell, and Q cannot be a stem cell because Q is the new specialised product, not the self-renewing parent.
options.C: Not correct. This is back to front. A differentiated cell cannot keep dividing to make stem cells, differentiation is normally one way.
options.D: Correct. P is the stem cell that self-renews, and Q is the differentiated cell produced for a specialised function.
